recipes.name: Potato Latkes
ingredients_raw: 1 large egg, beaten, or more to taste
0.5 teaspoon salt, or more to taste
0.25 cup peanut oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Grate potatoes in a food processor fitted with the grater attachment. Transfer to cheesecloth; wring well to remove as much moisture as possible.
Place 2 cups potatoes in a medium bowl (save any extra for another use). Add egg, flour, onion, and salt; stir until well combined.

Heat 1/4 inch of oil in a large, heavy-duty skillet over medium-high heat. Add large spoonfuls of potato mixture, pressing down to form 1/4- to 1/2-inch-thick patties. Cook until golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Potato Latkes
raw_recipe.description: This potato latke recipe is a classic, made with shredded potatoes, grated onion, and a flour-egg binder, then fried until golden and deliciously crisp.

review.reviewBody: What I like to do with these is to grate the potatoes, as opposed to shredding. I find the texture much more appealing. More like a potato pancake, instead of a true latkes, but that's just my personal preference. For every 2 cups of grated potato, one egg is really a sufficient binder, and any more than that just makes them too heavy. I also use alot less salt, but that again is to taste. Instead of the flour, I have also found better results substituting matzoh ball mix, which contains baking soda and seasonings. They seem to come out lighter, and more flavorful this way. Don't forget to add the grated onion... it's an absolute must in my opinion, and here again, I add twice as much. And I personally have never bothered with the cheesecloth thing. As you lift out spoonfuls, the moisture simply seeps to the bottom of the bowl. No problem. Don't wait for Hannukah to enjoy these treats, and don't forget the applesauce (or sour cream.) Enjoy!

I was in a hurry for a side so I used frozen tater tots. Thawed them in microwave and crushed them up and followed the recipe. They came out really good! My family liked them and it sure beat shredding the potatoes.
When you squeeze the liquid out of the potatoes reserve the liquid. Potato starch sinks to the bottom of the liquid. Toss the potato starch back into the latke mixture. You will prob need less flour.

(Update...) made these again in my husband's grandma's ancient waffle iron with a little olive oil spray. SO EASY, LESS MESSY, PROBABLY HEALTHIER. 


(first review) Wow! Followed other advice, tripled onion and only one egg. Added a tsp of baking powder and some garlic. These were awesome for husband and two toddlers. Will make again and figure out how to hide other veggies in them. Hubs liked the shredded potato better than other grated versions. Will heat up leftovers and put a runny egg on top for breakfast.

Made this last night. Delicious! Read other reviews and only used 1 egg, 3 T of grated onion. Grated 3 medium potatoes. Used vegetable oil. Must be very hot. Made 8 latkes which fed 4 adults. Just squeezed potatoes between paper towels worked perfect.
I used leftover mashed potatoes instead of the grated ones and it turned out delicious ...

You best change the amount of salt in this recipe! If I had put the 1.5 teaspoons that it called for I would have had to thrown them in the garbage but because I only put 1 teaspoon in and they were just edible (I had read the other reviews and their comments on salt). I only used 1 egg per 2 cups of grated potato (thanks to other reviewers). I also added a dash of baking powder. I also fried them in sunflower oil. Other than the salt issue and eggs, they turned out great!!

I didn’t follow this recipe but I did and have made traditional latkes for channuka. I made mine today with russets and nappa cabbage and onions this time, I wanted a breakfast patty so I also added three eggs, chia seeds, flax seed for added protien and used chick pea flour. I’m baking them hope they turn out. They’re delicious! Baked cut down on oil and calories.

I’ve been making them for decades from my mother in law’s recipe and have gotten compliments. What recipe here is missing is a good amount of pepper and it needs more onion, at least 1/4 cup for the three potatoes.
Draining the water from potatoes is key; I reduced the eggs. Doubled the recipe but only used 4 large eggs total. Salt after cooking.

I did shred the potatoes and grated the onions. No need for the cheesecloth. Just put the mixture between your hands and squeeze, letting all the moisture out. I also used 3 Tbs. grated onion, 1 egg, 3 Tbs. flour and fried it in half peanut oil and half canola oil. These have to be eaten as soon as they are off the frying pan and put on paper towls for a minute. Serve with Sour cream. Delicious!!!!!
Good
Followed recipe except for the peanut oil. Grandson is allergic. Used duck fat instead. Will definitely make this quite often.

I added two tablespoons of shredded carrot, two eggs instead of one, and a little bit more salt, about 1 and 1/2 teaspoons total. I also used rice oil instead of peanut as it is cheap where I live and it adds no flavor. Even with my poor cooking skills it turned out great!
Good for breakfast
The amount of salt suggested is perfect, unlike the review that suggests otherwise.
Delicious
Great, very delicious...!!

I make my latkes following this recipe usually every time, but depending on what I have to use sometimes instead of onion I use yelllow pepper,, garlic or w.e I have and aways turns out great especially with a scoop of sour cream on the side.
Added an extra tablespoon of onion , a teaspoon of green onion and a tablespoon of parsley...turned out great!
